Troubleshooting and limitations¶

Installation and command errors¶

uv cannot find the pinned Python

Update uv using the installation method you originally used, then retry uv sync --extra dev --locked. If your platform has no compatible interpreter or dependency wheel, inspect that package’s error rather than silently changing numerical dependencies. Python 3.14.10 is the tested pin; an arbitrary later minor version is not necessarily supported by every wheel.

ModuleNotFoundError or poly-mpm: command not found

From the checkout root, run uv sync --extra dev --locked and use uv run --locked python MPM.py ball. For a pip environment, activate it first. python -m pip may be absent from a uv-created environment; use uv sync to manage that environment.

The example cannot be imported

Use its module name, such as ball, rather than inputs/ball.py. Put new modules under inputs/ and expose Params(args). Run the documented commands from the checkout root.

IndexError while loading an example

Some legacy examples access positional arguments directly. Check the example matrix and supply every listed argument in order. Arguments are specific to the chosen input.

Unsupported material law

Check the exact registry name and Constitutive model audit. The retired elastic_time, ken_kamrin, and ken_simple implementations are not available. viscous_size and the separate legacy P.F compressible-fluid path are unimplemented. Four inputs remain deliberately unsupported: tunnel, poly_avalanche, tri_seg_test, and fluid.

Output and runtime¶

No plot window appears

Expected: figures are saved as PNGs. Check P.save_dir, the output flags, and whether the input replaces a default callback. output=False disables all output, including custom histories.

No files after a short preview

The preview may end before savetime, and an input’s custom callback may save only at save times. Set P.savetime=P.dt for a few steps and choose a separate directory, as in Getting started.

A run appears to take forever

Check dt, t_f, and plot frequency in the input. Some original examples request millions of steps. Start with run(..., max_steps=100, output=False). The CLI has no generic duration or maximum-step switch. Ctrl-C interrupts a run but does not create a restart checkpoint or guarantee end callbacks run.

A Matplotlib cache warning appears

Matplotlib needs a writable cache/config directory. If your home directory is read-only, set MPLCONFIGDIR to a writable directory before starting Python; for example on macOS/Linux, MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/poly-mpm-mpl uv run --locked python MPM.py ball.

Numerical errors¶

A particle leaves the domain

The solver fails before invalid cell lookup. Check domain extents, inlet/ outlet or periodic configuration, velocity and loading, then timestep. Moving beyond an unconstrained grid edge is not an implicit free-surface boundary extension or an automatically expanding computational domain.

A model reports nonfinite state

The error identifies the law, material, timestep, field, and particle rows. Check parameter units, initial conditions, model domain, and timestep. Reduce the timestep as a diagnostic, then perform convergence checks. Finite output alone is not proof of an accurate or physically valid solution.

Grain fractions do not sum to one

Initial rows must be nonnegative and sum to one. Use phi of shape (ns,) or (n, ns). The corrected segregation tests conserve species mass without clipping or renormalisation. Investigate inventory and boundary fluxes rather than enabling normalise_phi to hide drift.

What the solver currently does¶

This is a research solver with a regular 2D grid, bilinear particle-grid interpolation, explicit mechanics, and a shared nodal momentum field. It has no GIMP/B-spline interpolation, APIC, deformation-gradient volume evolution, independent multi-body contact, general curved boundaries, implicit/quasistatic solve, or checkpoint/restart. Particle mass and represented volume remain fixed; reconstructed density is a diagnostic, also used by the retained Pouliquen cutoff. The original five material laws retain legacy conventions; the four restored laws have separate physical corrections and analytical tests.

See NumPy array conversion, Constitutive model audit, and Source and correction of segregation drift for exact scope. Smoke-tested examples, equation checks, conservation tests, experimental validation, and convergence studies are different levels of evidence. Choose the evidence required for your application.

poly-mpm

2D material point method with grain-size segregation
